hypotheses.justification: It follows from hn : (n:ℝ) ≤ p, because 0 ≤ (n:ℝ) (Nat.cast_nonneg n), so 0 ≤ p. In the proof, hp is used only in `add_nonneg hp hP` and in `mul_le_mul hn hm (Nat.cast_nonneg m) hp`. Replace it there by `((Nat.cast_nonneg n).trans hn)`. The statement is unchanged and still true.

The product on the left contains the factor K, so the case K = 0 makes the left side 0, and 0 ≤ exp(...) holds. If K ≥ 1, then 1 ≤ K ≤ exp Q gives Q ≥ 0 (via Real.one_le_exp_iff or Real.exp_le_one_iff), so hQ is recovered. In the proof, hQ is used only in hKPow, in `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ... hQ`. Do a case split on K = 0 first. In the K = 0 case, simp reduces the left side to 0 and Real.exp_nonneg closes the goal. In the K ≥ 1 case, derive hQ from hK and continue as before. This does not need to be paired with deleting hp, so both can be deleted together. hP, by contrast, is genuinely needed: take H = 0, n = m = 0, d = 1, K = 1, Q = 0, p = 10 and P very negative. The left side is 1 and the right side is exp(p + (p+P+1) + p·p·P), which is tiny.
